sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Zone
FROM ops.zones z
WHERE z.LocationID NOT IN (SELECT t.RatecodeID FROM lake.trips t WHERE t.PULocationID = z.LocationID)
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query executes a correlated NOT IN subquery that forces a full scan of the 495k-row trips table for each of the 265 zones, performing a LEFT_DELIM_JOIN (anti-join) with a hash join build side that is rebuilt repeatedly due to the correlation on PULocationID = LocationID.

hypotheses.claim: NOT IN over a subquery forces a null-aware anti join, which is expensive. (matched: not in (select t.ratecodeid from lake.trips t where t.pulocationid = z.locationid) order b)

The LEFT_DELIM_JOIN (node 5) implements the NOT IN as a correlated anti-join, causing the inner hash join subtree (nodes 6-8) to be rebuilt or re-probed for every row from zones, resulting in O(zones × trips) work instead of a single hash anti-join.

The inner HASH_JOIN (node 7) builds a hash table on trips filtered by the correlated PULocationID value, but the optimizer fails to hoist the trips scan out of the correlation, so the same large table is scanned repeatedly.

The SEQ_SCAN on trips (node 8) reads all 495k rows with two columns for each zone; converting the NOT IN to a single uncorrelated LEFT ANTI JOIN or NOT EXISTS with a pre-aggregated distinct RatecodeID per PULocationID would allow one scan and one hash build.
